newsitem.title: INDONESIA: ICFTU leader meets jailed Indonesian labour head.
newsitem.headline: ICFTU leader meets jailed Indonesian labour head.

text.p: Detained Indonesian labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan was in good health, according to the general secretary of the International Confederation of Free Trade Unions (ICFTU), who visited him in his cell on Thursday.

Bill Jordan, who is leading a delegation of eight trade unionists from around the world on a fact-finding mission to Indonesia, said he met the jailed labour leader for 20 minutes in the presence of security officers.
"He's in good health. Our campaign to get him out of prison will continue. He looks well and says he's being treated well," Jordan told Reuters.

Pakpahan, head of the independent Indonesia Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), was arrested in connection with riots in Jakarta in July which left at least five people dead and scores of vehicles and buildings gutted by fire.
He was later charged with subversion, which carries a possible death penalty.
Jordan said they did not have time to talk in detail about the charges against Pakpahan, who is being held in a cell at the Attorney-General's office in Jakarta awaiting trial.

"We do not believe the charges," Jordan said. "Muchtar is a quiet man, a gentle man. We have never seen any evidence that he would act any way other than peacefully in the pursuance of the defence of working people."
The July 27 riots followed moves by police to evict supporters of former Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) leader Megawati Sukarnoputri from the party's headquarters.
Megawati, the daughter of Indonesia's late founding President Sukarno, was ousted as leader of the minority PDI by a government-backed faction at a congress in June.
She has filed a lawsuit, claiming her dismissal was illegal.
The government has blamed the riots on the small leftist People's Democratic Party (PRD) which they alleged was part of a communist plot to overthrow the state.
Pakpahan was originally arrested as part of an investigation into the PRD leader, Budiman Sudjatmiko, who is also being held on charges of subversion.
"We are very concerned that he's been arrested on trumped up charges ... charges that could not be sustained," Jordan said. "We will intensify our world campaign until he is out ..."

The ICFTU, which represents around 124 million trade unionists around the world, is considering membership applications from both Pakpahan's SBSI and the government-sanctioned All Indonesian Workers' Union (SPSI), Jordan said.
